title: Kernel-probe router with proportional latency buckets for token-phase arbitration
creator: Lina Chen
description:
Problem statement: current phase arbitration treats prefill and decode phases independently of kernel performance characteristics. That leads to suboptimal routing when some model variants hit slower kernels (e.g., cross-attention transpose on older SM architectures) and causes either latency spikes for latency-sensitive tenants or throughput regressions when the allocator aggressively hedges.

Proposal summary: implement a lightweight kernel-probe router that attaches a short kernel performance fingerprint to warm clients and uses that signal to place tokens into proportional latency buckets at admission time. Combine this with small per-bucket "fairness buffers" that ensure lower-priority phases (usually large prefill requests) get serviced proportionally when the system is near saturation. The router is strictly advisory for the existing arbiter and uses a conservative backoff policy—no forced preemption—so it should be safe to roll out behind a feature flag.

Key components and design decisions:
- Kernel-probe fingerprint: on first few warm requests or when an ephemeral mismatch is detected, run a micro-benchmark (milliseconds-scale) to estimate per-stage kernel timings (prefill, KV-cache apply, decode token). Store an anonymized signature in the client routing context.
- Proportional latency buckets: admission assigns incoming request phases to fine-grained latency buckets (e.g., <20ms, 20-50ms, 50-120ms, >120ms) based on kernel fingerprint + input size. Buckets drive token prioritization weights and small time-slice quotas.
- Fairness buffers: short-lived credits added to lower-priority buckets to avoid starvation; credits accumulate when system is underutilized and provide guaranteed minimum allocation during bursts. Buffer sizing tuned by historical arrival curves per model family.
- Kernel-informed opportunistic fast-paths: when a fingerprint indicates compatible optimized kernels, allow opportunistic coalescing and larger batch sizes for decode stages without breaching latency SLOs.
- Latency vs throughput knob: expose a per-tenant policy that shifts bucket weights (latency-first vs throughput-first) and a global safety floor that prevents throughput-first policies from starving critical prefill workloads.
- Safety & rollout: router returns a routing score; arbiter makes final decision. Feature toggles per-region/model. Canary rollout with synthetic and live traffic checks.

Metrics to track:
- p50/p95/p99 tail latency for prefill and decode broken out by kernel fingerprint
- tokens/sec and GPU utilization per bucket
- fairness buffer consumption and credit refill rates
- spillover ratio (requests routed to fallback kernels)
- regressions in throughput for throughput-first tenants

Implementation plan (high level):
1) kernel-probe micro-benchmark lib (0.5 sprint) + proto for fingerprint in request context
2) admission layer changes to add proportional buckets and credits (1 sprint)
3) arbiter advisory API + feature flags (0.5 sprint)
4) end-to-end e2e tests and benchmarking harness (1 sprint)
5) canary rollout, dashboards, and tweak (1 sprint)

Rollout criteria:
- No >5% increase in p95 latency for latency-first tenants during canary
- Throughput regressions within 3% for throughput-first tenants after tuning
- No increase in OOM or kernel failure rates

Open trade-offs and unresolved questions:
- Frequency and cost of kernel-probes vs staleness of fingerprint for dynamic heterogenous clusters. We should weigh occasional microbenchmarks against cache staleness.
- Privacy: what to store in fingerprints; keep minimal and non-identifying.
- Fairness buffer sizing: empirical tuning vs model-family heuristics.

2025-02-20 - Marco Alvarez (review): Suggest we limit micro-benchmark to <3ms on average. Also flagged potential interference with kernel autograd caches—recommend probe on dedicated warmup slots.
2025-02-24 - Noah Brooks: Updated design to move micro-bench to warmup slots and added conservative backoff. Added release target runtime-1.21.
2025-02-27 - SRE: Need explicit instrumentation to correlate GPU SM occupancy with bucket assignments. Added as dependency for rollout checks.
2025-03-01 - PM (Amira Hassan): Confirmed customer impact medium; requested that latency-first tenants have an escape hatch (immediate bypass of router) in UI.

2025-03-04 - Lina Chen: Implemented probe lib prototype and basic bucket logic in branch eng/kerprobe. Running synthetic bench; early results show 6% throughput gain for compatible fingerprints and no latency regression in synthetic latency-first profiles. Preparing PR for review.
